title: The Lord, My God, Be Praised
description: The Lord, My God, Be Praised in Tonic Solfa to WAS FRAG ICH NACH DER WELT, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Johann Olearius wrote these words in German. August Crull's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 272.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked 6.7.6.7.6.6.6.6, to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WAS FRAG ICH NACH DER WELT; any other 6.7.6.7.6.6.6.6 tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Lord, my God, be praised, My Light, my Life from hea_-ven; My Mak-er, who to me Hath soul and bo-dy giv_-en; My Fa-ther, who pro-tects My life from in-fan-cy And might-y gifts of love Hath e’er be-stowed on me.

lines: The Lord, my God, be praised,
My Light, my Life from heaven;
The Lord, my God, be praised,
My Trust, my Life from heaven,
Whose life for me was given;
The Lord, my God, be praised,
My Hope, my Life from heaven,
The Son to me hath given;
And gives me strength and power,
The Lord, my God, be praised,
The Lord, my God, be praised,
In whose great name I boast,
To Him we now sing praise,
The Lord, my God, be praised

licence: Public domain: Johann Olearius died in 1684; August Crull died in 1923.
credits: Words by Johann Olearius (1611–1684), translated by August Crull (1845–1923), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to WAS FRAG ICH NACH DER WELT by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
